# FractalPark

> FractalPark is an open-source, formula-first fractal knowledge and creation platform with growing Fractint-compatible FRM support, working to bring Fractint’s formula heritage into the modern browser.

## Overview

FractalPark is a free, open-source (MIT) WebGL application that renders entirely in the browser. Anyone can explore, learn, and create mathematical fractal art without installation or an account; saving artworks and custom formulas uses email one-time-code sign-in and a private cloud library, and publishing to the community gallery is always explicit. The default entry point is Explore, the interactive fractal workspace.

## Pages

- [Explore](https://www.fractalpark.com/en/explore): Default landing and interactive fractal workspace with 94 formulas, real-time controls, URL sharing, and PNG export
- [Formula Atlas](https://www.fractalpark.com/en/formulas): Directory of 94 built-in formulas across 7 families, linking to 21 in-depth Formula Guides
- [FRM Guide](https://www.fractalpark.com/en/formulas/frm): Fractint-compatible FRM language guide — development, support matrix, core syntax, and tutorials
- [FRM Editor](https://www.fractalpark.com/en/formulas/editor): Standalone FRM authoring workflow with import, diagnostics, and preview
- [Gallery](https://www.fractalpark.com/en/gallery): Published preset collection, community gallery, and the owner's cloud artworks
- [Drift](https://www.fractalpark.com/en/drift): Immersive full-viewport preset slideshow (experiential page; marked `noindex, follow`, excluded from the sitemap)
- [About](https://www.fractalpark.com/en/about): Project facts, current boundaries, future directions, and open-source details

## Core Features

- **94 Built-in Formulas**: Mandelbrot, Julia, Burning Ship, Tricorn, Phoenix, Newton, Magnet, Lambda, McMullen, rational, transcendental, and more, across 7 families
- **21 Formula Guides**: In-depth bilingual guides with math, history, visual character, and live examples
- **Fractint-compatible FRM**: Custom formula editor using Fractint-style .frm compatibility and FractalPark native directives with real-time compilation (a growing, tested subset — not a complete Fractint reimplementation)
- **7 Transform Plugins**: Kaleidoscope, Mobius, Inversion, Polar, Sinusoidal, Spherical, None
- **Coloring System**: 9 coloring modes with orbit channel support
- **Real-time Rendering**: WebGL GPU acceleration with SSAA options
- **High-res Export**: PNG export with tiled rendering for large images, up to 4x
- **Cloud Library**: Artworks and custom formulas saved behind email one-time-code sign-in (no passwords); anonymous creation stays fully usable
- **Community Gallery**: Explicit publishing under CC BY 4.0; artworks using a custom formula also publish the formula source under MIT
- **Multilingual**: Interface in English, Simplified Chinese, Portuguese, Korean, Russian, Spanish, and French

## URL Parameters

Fractal state is URL-serializable. The live schema uses compact keys from `src/lib/url-params.ts`.

Core view:
- `cx`, `cy`: center coordinates
- `z`: zoom level
- `rot`: rotation in radians
- `iter`: max iterations

Formula and Julia:
- `fm`: formula ID or short key (`m`, `bs`, `tr`, `ph`; omitted means Mandelbrot)
- `julia`: `1` or `0`
- `jre`, `jim`: Julia constant real/imaginary parts
- `pow`: power for formulas that support it

Color and render:
- `pal`: palette index
- `oc`: outside coloring (`sm`, `ot`, `st`, `bi`, `ti` or full plugin ID)
- `ic`: inside coloring (`bk`, `fo`, `ad` or full plugin ID)
- `grad`: custom gradient stops as `position:hex,position:hex`
- `ssaa`: `1` enables SSAA
- `ait`: `1` enables adaptive iterations

Transforms, lighting, and animation:
- `tr`: transform plugin ID
- `pp`: plugin parameters as `name:value,name:value`
- `ots`, `otx`, `oty`, `otr`, `otw`: orbit trap shape/position/radius/width
- `lg`, `lgm`, `lga`, `lge`, `lgi`: lighting controls
- `kf`: keyframes as `cx,cy,z,rot|cx,cy,z,rot`

Example:
https://www.fractalpark.com/en/explore?cx=-0.5&cy=0.25&z=12.50&fm=burningShip&oc=st&julia=1&jre=-0.620000&jim=0.410000&pal=1

Full documentation: https://www.fractalpark.com/llms-full.txt
